added_models.model: Skeletally mature cynomolgus monkeys, 1-year pegbelfermin toxicology (bone)

safety.population: Adult male cynomolgus monkeys, pegbelfermin 0.3 or 0.75 mg/kg weekly for 1 year (0.7-2.2x human AUC at 20 mg weekly), n=5/group
safety.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. The abstract states the exposure margin against the human 20 mg weekly dose and predicts low bone risk in adults, but reports no GI or clinical-sign data, so the monkey stays silent on the class's diarrhoea.
safety.judgement: Model entry. A second bone model on a member drug, built to answer the Wei 2012 mouse prediction at clinically matched exposures; it predicts no bone harm with a stated margin.
safety.model: Skeletally mature cynomolgus monkeys, 1-year pegbelfermin toxicology (bone)
safety.note: One year of pegbelfermin at 0.7-2.2x the human 20 mg weekly AUC left bone biomarkers, densitometry and strength unchanged in adult monkeys.
safety.short: No bone toxicity after 1 year, margin stated
safety.quote: There were no PGBF-related effects on bone biomarkers, radiography, densitometry, or strength.

safety.magnitude_basis: bone mineral density by DXA: predicted no change (1-year monkey) vs no change at 12-16 weeks of pegbelfermin
safety.population: NASH F1-F3 patients at 16 weeks (NCT02413372) and obese T2D patients at 12 weeks (NCT02097277); monkey margin benchmarked to 20 mg weekly
safety.confidence_note: Year 2021 is the monkey paper's online date (2021-08-06), when the pairing first became possible; the patient-side sentence (Kaufman 2020) summarises Sanyal 2019 and Charles 2019 DXA. FALCON 1, 48 weeks at the benchmarked 20 mg weekly dose, posted no bone outcome and its paper reports none. Whether the paywalled discussion itself cites the clinical BMD is unverified.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction, not a prospective match: the 0.3/0.75 mg/kg doses were chosen to bracket the human 20 mg weekly AUC, a dose fixed after the 2018 phase 2a, when 12- and 16-week BMD were already known, and publication followed Kaufman 2020. It reproduced the human absence of bone loss, so retro; a prospective bone comparison would need FALCON's 48-week DXA, which is unreported.
safety.model: Skeletally mature cynomolgus monkeys, 1-year pegbelfermin toxicology (bone)
safety.note: Monkeys at clinically matched exposure for a year showed no bone effect, reproducing the no-BMD-change seen in 12-16-week pegbelfermin patients.
safety.quote: No change in mean bone mineral density was observed following 12 weeks or 16 weeks of pegbelfermin treatment.
safety.reason: Reproduced absent bone loss, after the fact

added_models.model: Sprague Dawley rats, 4- and 26-week efruxifermin toxicology

safety.population: Male and female Sprague Dawley rats, weekly efruxifermin at supra-pharmacological doses for 4 or 26 weeks
safety.confidence_note: Open access, full text read. The studies were run before publication (GLP toxicology supporting the clinical programme) but no run dates are given; first use is dated to the paper. No NOAEL or exposure margin is stated, so no dose entry.
safety.judgement: Model entry. The rat was used to test the harms that translated inconsistently for other FGF21 analogues (blood pressure, sympathetic tone, urine volume); it predicted none for efruxifermin and, separately, increased food intake.
safety.model: Sprague Dawley rats, 4- and 26-week efruxifermin toxicology
safety.note: Chronic efruxifermin in rats cut weight gain despite more food intake, lowered urine volume, and left sympathetic and corticosterone markers unchanged.
safety.short: Rats: no sympathetic activation, more food intake
safety.quote: Markers of sympathetic activation, urinary corticosterone and ratio of adrenal-to-body weight were unchanged.

safety.magnitude_basis: systemic blood pressure and cortisol/sympathetic markers: predicted no rise, none seen in T2D (Kaufman 2020) and NASH (Harrison 2021) patients
safety.population: T2D patients up to 70 mg weekly (Kaufman 2020) and NASH F1-F3 patients up to 70 mg weekly for 16 weeks (BALANCED, NCT03976401)
safety.confidence_note: Registry date is BALANCED's (NCT03976401, results 2022-08-04); the efruxifermin phase 1 MAD (Kaufman 2020) cites no CT.gov record. Retro rather than same because the stated comparison was written after both human results were published and the rat run dates are not given; if the 26-week study predates the phase 1 BP data the entry would be same.
safety.judgement: The paper itself sets the rat sympathetic/corticosterone result beside the unchanged blood pressure and salivary cortisol in efruxifermin-treated humans (stated comparison). The rats' increased food intake also matches the increased-appetite adverse event in Kaufman 2020, but the paper does not state that pairing, so it is not scored. Blood pressure is a harm the class had shown with PF-05231023, so the prediction was load-bearing.
safety.model: Sprague Dawley rats, 4- and 26-week efruxifermin toxicology
safety.note: Paper states the rats' unchanged sympathetic markers mirror unchanged blood pressure and salivary cortisol in efruxifermin-treated T2D and NASH patients.
safety.short: Rat no-BP-rise mirrors patients, stated after
safety.quote: The absence of an increase in sympathetic tone in rats mirrors the unchanged salivary cortisol and systemic blood pressure following efruxifermin treatment in humans.
safety.reason: Mirrors unchanged human BP, stated after result

added_models.model: FGF21 rs838133 and truncating-variant carriers (UK Biobank human genetics)

safety.population: 451,099 UK Biobank participants, FGF21 rs838133 A allele (putative reduced FGF21 function)
safety.confidence_note: Open access; abstract read. The paper states its aim is to use the human allele to anticipate adverse and beneficial effects of targeting FGF21, so it was offered as a model for the class.
safety.judgement: Model entry. A natural experiment in reduced FGF21 signalling: carriers have higher blood pressure, so agonism should not raise it, the harm PF-05231023 had shown. No drug in the model (product_in_model false).
safety.model: FGF21 rs838133 and truncating-variant carriers (UK Biobank human genetics)
safety.note: The FGF21 A allele tracks higher blood pressure and waist-hip ratio with lower body fat, offered to predict effects of targeting FGF21.
safety.short: Lower-FGF21 allele carriers have higher BP
safety.quote: We then showed that this allele is more strongly associated with higher blood pressure and waist-hip ratio, despite an association with lower total body-fat percentage, than it is with BMI or type 2 diabetes.

safety.magnitude_basis: blood pressure: carriers of lower-function variants have higher BP, so agonism predicted no rise; efruxifermin PK-PD showed no association with BP
safety.population: Type 2 diabetes patients, efruxifermin multiple ascending doses up to 140 mg weekly (phase 1, Kaufman 2020)
safety.confidence_note: Full text read. Kaufman 2020 cites no CT.gov record for its phase 1 MAD (the NCT numbers in the paper are PF-05231023 trials and BALANCED), so registry_date is null. Comparison made in T2D patients, imported to MASH as safety transfers. The rat paper (Tillman 2022) restates the same consistency.
safety.judgement: The genetic prior (2018) predates the efruxifermin phase 1 result and the source states the comparison: the absence of a blood-pressure rise is 'consistent with' carrier phenotypes. Scored same, direction only; a lowering of BP, which the genetics might also have predicted, was not seen either.
safety.model: FGF21 rs838133 and truncating-variant carriers (UK Biobank human genetics)
safety.note: Efruxifermin left blood pressure unchanged in T2D patients, which Kaufman 2020 calls consistent with the BP phenotype of FGF21 variant carriers.
safety.short: No BP rise, as carrier genetics predicted
safety.quote: The predicted lack of effect of AKR-001 on blood pressure is consistent with the observed blood pressure phenotypes of human carriers of FGF21 genetic variants.
safety.reason: Carrier BP phenotype matched: no rise

added_models.model: Diet-induced obese mice given recombinant human FGF21 (bone, Amgen)

safety.population: High-fat-diet DIO mice, rhFGF21 0.1-3 mg/kg daily for 2 weeks; FGF21 knockout mice
safety.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. Native rhFGF21, not a member drug (product_in_model false); Amgen authors (Stanislaus) overlap with the efruxifermin discovery group.
safety.judgement: Model entry. The newer mouse model that contradicted Wei 2012 on bone; per the brief a model that did better is its own track rather than a correction of the failed one.
safety.model: Diet-induced obese mice given recombinant human FGF21 (bone, Amgen)
safety.note: Two weeks of rhFGF21 in DIO mice improved metabolism without any bone loss by DXA, micro-CT or histomorphometry; FGF21 knockouts had normal bone.
safety.short: No bone loss with rhFGF21 in DIO mice
safety.quote: However, bone loss was not detected in rhFGF21-treated mice by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), micro-CT, and histomorphometric analyses.

safety.magnitude_basis: bone mineral density by DXA: predicted no loss vs no change at 12-16 weeks of pegbelfermin
safety.population: NASH F1-F3 patients at 16 weeks (NCT02413372) and obese T2D patients at 12 weeks (NCT02097277)
safety.confidence_note: Kaufman 2020 sets the DIO-mouse rhFGF21 no-bone-loss result (its ref 27) directly before the pegbelfermin BMD sentence quoted, without a verdict. The same 12-16-week DXA caveats as the mouse-fgf21-gain-of-function track apply: NCT02413372 femoral-neck changes are small and noisy, and 16 weeks is short for bone.
safety.judgement: Prospective: the mouse result (2016) precedes any member-drug BMD datum (2018). Matched in direction (no loss predicted, none seen), so same; one source states the comparison but calls the preclinical picture inconsistent rather than resolved.
safety.model: Diet-induced obese mice given recombinant human FGF21 (bone, Amgen)
safety.note: Kaufman 2020 pairs the DIO-mouse rhFGF21 no-bone-loss finding with unchanged BMD after 12-16 weeks of pegbelfermin in T2D and NASH patients.
safety.quote: No change in mean bone mineral density was observed following 12 weeks or 16 weeks of pegbelfermin treatment.
safety.reason: Predicted no bone loss; none seen

added_models.model: Pegozafermin population PK/PD exposure-response model (phase 1b/2a NASH data, in silico)

dose.population: Model fitted to the phase 1b/2a NASH MAD study (NCT04048135); simulations of 30 mg weekly and 44 mg every 2 weeks
dose.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. Year 2021 is a proxy: the paper (online 2023-10-02) says its simulations provided the rationale for the ENLIVEN doses, and ENLIVEN started 2021-06-04, so the model was built and used before then.
dose.judgement: Model entry. An in-silico exposure-response model used to choose the phase 2b regimens; its stated target is an average concentration giving near-full HFF effect at 30 mg weekly, with 44 mg every 2 weeks as an effective alternative.
dose.model: Pegozafermin population PK/PD exposure-response model (phase 1b/2a NASH data, in silico)
dose.note: PK/PD simulations predicted 30 mg weekly approximates the full liver-fat effect and 44 mg every 2 weeks is effective; both chosen for ENLIVEN.
dose.short: Simulations picked 30 mg QW, 44 mg Q2W
dose.quote: Simulations showed that the 30 mg q.w. dose approximated the full PD effect; almost all patients would benefit from a greater than or equal to 30% HFF reduction, suggesting fibrosis regression.

dose.magnitude_basis: the two simulated regimens (30 mg weekly, 44 mg every 2 weeks) were the ENLIVEN arms and both met the fibrosis primary
dose.confidence_note: Pairing: ENLIVEN (online 2023-06-24) and the model paper (2023-10-02) do not cite each other at abstract level. Year 2023 is when the model side became public. The model stated no tolerability margin (margin_stated false).
dose.judgement: Not a retrodiction: the model was built from the 2019-2021 phase 1b/2a data and fixed the ENLIVEN regimens before the trial started, even though it was published after the result. Reached, drug worked: both simulated regimens were dosed as planned and improved fibrosis, so same.
dose.model: Pegozafermin population PK/PD exposure-response model (phase 1b/2a NASH data, in silico)
dose.note: ENLIVEN dosed exactly the simulated regimens, 30 mg weekly and 44 mg every 2 weeks, and both improved fibrosis at 24 weeks.
dose.quote: In this phase 2b trial, treatment with pegozafermin led to improvements in fibrosis.

efficacy.population: Model fitted to the phase 1b/2a NASH MAD study (NCT04048135); simulated hepatic fat fraction response
efficacy.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. Year 2021 is a proxy for when the simulations were used (before ENLIVEN's 2021-06-04 start); the paper is from 2023. The model's own readout is HFF, a surrogate it links to fibrosis regression.
efficacy.judgement: Model entry. The prediction was that almost all patients at 30 mg weekly would reach a >=30% HFF reduction, which the authors read as fibrosis regression.
efficacy.model: Pegozafermin population PK/PD exposure-response model (phase 1b/2a NASH data, in silico)
efficacy.note: Simulations predicted a >=30% liver-fat reduction in almost all patients at 30 mg weekly, taken as a signal of fibrosis regression.
efficacy.quote: Simulations showed that the 30 mg q.w. dose approximated the full PD effect; almost all patients would benefit from a greater than or equal to 30% HFF reduction, suggesting fibrosis regression.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: predicted HFF response (surrogate, read as fibrosis regression) vs the fibrosis-improvement primary endpoint met at both simulated regimens
efficacy.confidence_note: Pairing at abstract level. The model predicted a surrogate (HFF); ENLIVEN's primary was histological fibrosis improvement, met at 30 mg weekly (22%) and 44 mg every 2 weeks (27%) vs placebo (7%) in the NEJM abstract. The HFF responder proportion in ENLIVEN was not checked, so the magnitude is direction only.
efficacy.judgement: The model's prediction was made before the trial and the primary responded at the regimens it chose, so same. It is a surrogate-to-histology prediction, hence direction_only; outcome_tested stays null (no outcome trial).
efficacy.model: Pegozafermin population PK/PD exposure-response model (phase 1b/2a NASH data, in silico)
efficacy.note: ENLIVEN's fibrosis primary was met at both regimens the model simulated as giving near-full liver-fat effect.
efficacy.quote: In this phase 2b trial, treatment with pegozafermin led to improvements in fibrosis.
efficacy.reason: Fibrosis primary met at simulated regimens

considered_not_added: Pegozafermin diabetic cynomolgus monkeys + healthy-volunteer SAD (JPET 2023, doi 10.1124/jpet.123.001618): same system as the draft's obese-diabetic-cyno-monkey track, already its model_src; a stated monkey-to-human comparison that strengthens that track, not a new one.
Pegozafermin phase 1b/2a in NASH patients (Loomba 2022, Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol, NCT04048135): patient data, not a model; it is the data the popPK/PD model was fitted to.

Kaufman 2020's own PK-PD model of efruxifermin heart rate / blood pressure (threshold predicted between 70 and 140 mg weekly): an in-human model built on the same phase 1 data; no later source found that sets its heart-rate threshold beside the 28/50 mg phase 2 results, so no comparison to score.

Non-member FGF21 analogues with tier-1 stated model-to-human comparisons: PF-05231023 (Talukdar 2016 monkeys/rats, raised BP and heart rate in humans; Kim 2017), LY2405319 (Gaich 2013 diabetic monkeys), zalfermin (2024-2025 mouse MASH), efimosfermin/MK-3655: outside the member list, so set aside per the brief.

Ex-vivo or patient-derived systems (patient organoids, precision-cut liver slices, primary human hepatocytes or adipocytes, PDX): the Europe PMC search returned reviews only; no member drug was tested in such a system against patient results.
Human challenge models: none exist for this class.

Mouse NASH/fibrosis models for efruxifermin or pegozafermin: no primary paper in the TITLE searches; the only member fibrosis model (pegbelfermin, Krupinski 2016 abstract) is already the nash-fibrosis-mouse track.

PNPLA3-genotype analysis of efruxifermin phase 2b trials (Hepatology 2026, doi 10.1097/hep.0000000000001792): a post-hoc patient stratification of trial results, not a model system predicting who responds.
Cell-based FGFR1c/KLB receptor-activation assays (pegozafermin JPET 2023; Fc-FGF21 expression-system comparison 2025): potency assays with no patient comparison.
FDA/EMA reviews: none; manifest.csv lists 'no NDA/BLA' for all three members, so regulator reliance on model data could not arise.
Rat toxicology dose/margin entry: Tillman 2022 states no NOAEL or exposure margin (full text grepped), so decision 16 cannot be applied; safety only.

Monkey 1-year study on GI harms: the abstract reports no clinical-sign or GI data and the paper is paywalled, so the monkey track's silence on diarrhoea/nausea stays unscored; FALCON 1 reported no bone outcome, so no prospective bone comparison at 48 weeks exists.

gaps.lead: Member-drug monkey bone model with a stated margin: pegbelfermin 1-year skeletally-mature cynomolgus study (Toxicol Appl Pharmacol 2021, doi 10.1016/j.taap.2021.115673, PMID 34364948) at 0.7-2.2x human AUC (20 mg QW) found no bone effects and states 'low potential for negative effects on bone quality in adult humans'. A second bone track (margin_stated true); retro vs same depends on when the study was run (rule question 4).
gaps.detail: cyno-monkey-1yr-bone-tox, safety (untested 2021, retro 2021, margin stated); retro vs same is rule question 4

gaps.lead: Member-drug rat BP/sympathetic model: efruxifermin 4/26-week Sprague Dawley tox (Br J Pharmacol 2022, doi 10.1111/bph.15725, PMID 34773249) states 'absence of an increase in sympathetic tone in rats mirrors the unchanged salivary cortisol and systemic blood pressure following efruxifermin treatment in humans' (Kaufman 2020 PK-PD). Stated comparison, published after the human data: retro. Rats also ate more, matching the increased-appetite AE.
gaps.detail: sd-rat-chronic-tox, safety (untested 2022, retro 2022 on Tillman 2022's stated comparison with Kaufman 2020)

gaps.lead: Human-genetic model on blood pressure: Kaufman 2020 (doi 10.1016/j.xcrm.2020.100057) compares the absence of a BP effect of efruxifermin with FGF21 loss-of-function variant carriers having higher BP (its ref 28); model_kind human_genetic, no track.

Monkey-track safety silence: tremor (Kaufman 2020: product-related withdrawals for tremor at 140 mg QW efruxifermin) and GI AEs (diarrhoea/nausea, the class's commonest harm) are harms a cynomolgus monkey could show; Stanislaus 2017 / Rosenstock 2023 say nothing. No safety entry exists on the obese-diabetic-cyno-monkey track; the pegbelfermin 1-year monkey paper (clinical observations, food intake) could settle whether monkeys predicted GI effects.
gaps.detail: Pegbelfermin 1-year monkey paper (PMID 34364948) is paywalled and its abstract reports no GI or tremor signs; Stanislaus 2017/Rosenstock 2023 state none, so no monkey GI/tremor prediction exists to score

gaps.lead: Later mouse bone model that reversed Wei 2012: Kaufman 2020 ref 27, a DIO-mouse rhFGF21 study finding no bone loss (likely Li et al., J Bone Miner Res 2017, Amgen); a separate track or a retrodiction on the bone question, absent from the draft.
gaps.detail: dio-mouse-rhfgf21-bone, safety (untested 2016 Li 2017, same 2020 Kaufman 2020; checker dates the same to 2018)
